population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈276M. Current users are 36.5% (≈100.7M), up 8.0 pts. Ever-used is 49.0% (≈135.2M), up 9.0 pts against a limit of 11. That leaves 12.5 pts (≈34.5M) who used and are off now, and ≈140.8M who have never used. Cycling arithmetic: about 19 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (19 + 5)/49.0 ≈ 49.0% have cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year, with the restart rate pushed up because the 50 mg pill makes restarting a pharmacy errand rather than a titration ordeal. Age check: 18–29: 21% × 52M = 10.9M; 30–49: 41.3% × 92M = 38.0M; 50–64: 52% × 62M = 32.2M; 65+: 28% × 70M = 19.6M. Total ≈ 100.7M = 36.5%. Income thirds average (41 + 37 + 31.5)/3 = 36.5. Growth came despite stalled prices and employer retreat, through five channels. (1) Ageing into the fixed-price Part D benefit. (2) The AUD indication (Jan 2036) plus earlier off-label EAP prescribing, ≈3.1M users whose primary coded reason is alcohol, about 40% of them below BMI 30. Many of these entered through mental-health parity after their employers dropped weight coverage. (3) Guideline-endorsed compulsion use, ≈1.2M. (4) 'Calm/focus/unhooked' cash subscriptions, up from 4.6M to ≈7.2M. (5) Imports, up from 7.1M to ≈12.1M. Under-30 growth (15.5→21%) is mostly cash subscriptions and AUD/gambling coding, not obesity. The middle third lost the most employer coverage and backfilled with cash pills and AUD coding. The bottom third grew on Medicaid in the 31 states plus DC and on imports. Off-now people (≈34.5M) are concentrated among workers whose plans dropped obesity coverage in the 2035–36 plan years and who had no qualifying diabetes, cardiac or AUD code, plus older users on bone pauses or post-NAION stops. Pediatric use is 1.4% of ≈73M ≈ 1.0M, mostly adolescents 12+. The adolescent bone readout was published in 2035 with mixed results (see ledger). About one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms of the Part D obesity benefit are unchanged: $199/month, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. AUD-indicated semaglutide is covered under Part D at the same negotiated rate from Mar 2036. Medicare pays 20.5% of fills, ≈20.6M users (≈18.9M aged 65+ and ≈1.7M disabled under-65): ≈8.6M for diabetes or cardiac codes and ≈12.0M on the obesity benefit. Obesity-benefit spend: 12.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $28.7B gross. Beneficiaries pay 12.0M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.2B, leaving ≈$21.5B for the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 20.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $49.2B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC use the 90% match and the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 14.5% of fills, ≈14.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $34.9B gross before supplemental rebates. Medicaid SUD benefits cover the AUD indication in all 50 states, including non-expansion states that do not cover obesity, and this is becoming the back door for low-income users in Texas, Florida and Georgia.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic 14–50 mg oral semaglutide since 2035. The Telangana first-filer plant is still under US import alert. China supplies API for most of the world's semaglutide and tirzepatide copies and sells 'research' retatrutide. Canada sells generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75, and generic oral semaglutide launched there in 2035. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt are expanding generic production. In the US, the mid-2035 contingent entry date for rival filers was triggered, but a Delaware preliminary injunction on a later-expiring device and formulation patent blocked launch pending Federal Circuit appeal.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: no portal price has changed since the 2033 increase. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide cost $249–329 direct. The Wegovy pill 50 mg is $299 direct. Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are $149–150 on the federal portal. Retatrutide is $449 direct and $1,649 list, amycretin $499, MariTide $549. PBM net is ≈$195–215. Payer mix of ≈100.7M users: commercial 29.5% (29.7M, roughly flat in absolute terms but now mostly diabetes, cardiac, OSA, CKD and AUD codes; ≈1.9M are AUD-coded); Medicare 20.5% (20.6M); Medicaid 14.5% (14.6M); cash/direct 23.5% (23.7M, including ≈7.2M 'calm', 'focus' and 'unhooked' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 12.0% (12.1M). Sum = 100% = 100.7M. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 64% to 46% of employers. Nearly all remaining plans are gated, and ≈40% use connected-cap or pharmacy-PDC adherence verification under the 2035 tri-agency wellness rule. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Routes: ≈47% of users are on daily orals, up from ≈36%. Injectables keep the top-efficacy tier (tirzepatide, retatrutide, MariTide).

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder in adults (semaglutide: Wegovy pill 50 mg and Wegovy 2.4 mg, approved Jan 2036; filed Dec 2034)
gambling disorder and compulsive buying disorder: guideline-endorsed, not FDA-approved (APA practice guideline, May 2036, second-line after CBT)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'unhooked' subscriptions on $149 oral starter doses (≈7.2M subscribers), including gambling- and shopping-craving tiers marketed after the APA guideline
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial completed enrolment; no filing)
compulsive screen use and compulsive sexual behaviour, prescribed by telehealth psychiatry under the compulsion guideline's 'related disorders' language
'metabolic health' and longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
AUD-coded prescribing for heavy drinkers below DSM threshold, a known coding route around employer obesity exclusions
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity holds through an existing product, not a new launch. The 50 mg Wegovy pill (approved Feb 2034, 16.4% vs 16.1% injectable) became the most-dispensed incretin in the US by late 2035, and the AUD sNDA was filed on it and on the 2.4 mg injection. Lilly's next-generation orals stay in development and unfiled; one entered phase 3 in 2035 and is not on the market. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Jun 2035. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 with no filing. The smoking SHAPS trial finished enrolment, with a readout due 2037. The compulsion indication is realised through guideline endorsement because no sponsor has filed. Novo has a phase 3 gambling-disorder trial enrolling. No US generic: the mid-2035 contingent date was blocked by injunction. Incretin market ≈$232B in 2036. US ≈$210B: (100.7M − 12.1M imports) = 88.6M paying users × ≈$198 average net × 12 ≈ $210.5B. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding to generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and leading cause of voluntary stops. In AUD-indicated users, early nausea overlaps with withdrawal symptoms and complicates assessment.
Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ base and high-dose regimens.
No causal confirmation. Heavy-drinking AUD users carry high baseline pancreatitis risk, which makes signal separation harder. Counterfeit dosing errors still confound reports.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; AUD label adds a caution for patients with a history of alcohol-related pancreatitis; MDL ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈2.1M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-dose labels; CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 9.5M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 20,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 total. The vertebral tail among cycling women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo settled in 2035 for an undisclosed sum with no label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4 per 100,000 baseline across ≈100.7M users, that is roughly 2,800 excess cases a year, mostly partial permanent monocular loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions (May 2034) on all products including AUD and low-dose starters; MDL consolidated 2035; bellwether trials scheduled 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association. Re-examined in AUD trial populations with high baseline psychiatric comorbidity; still null.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening / anhedonia ('Ozempic personality', 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded and labelled Oct 2035. A pooled re-analysis of SHAPS and PHQ secondary endpoints across semaglutide, tirzepatide and oral trials found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~4.8% of users at standard weight-loss doses vs ~2.1% on placebo, and ~2.5% vs ~2.0% at low oral starter doses, which is not statistically distinct. Observational data give ~12% at 12 mg retatrutide. Across ≈100.7M users, if causal, that is on the order of 2.5–3M excess cases. Dose-dependent; mostly resolves within 8 weeks of stopping.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Added to Adverse Reactions with a prevalence table and Medication Guide language ('reduced interest or pleasure'), class-wide. Not a Warning. Telehealth 'calm' brands must display it. FTC consent orders still bar anxiety-treatment claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2035–36 employer coverage drops produced the largest wave of non-medical stops since the 2033 shortage, mostly in middle-income workers without qualifying codes.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code applies to Medicare only; the Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver in 2035, so 12-month lockouts stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users and in import users with no clinical contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent bone readout showed slower BMD accrual (~0.3 SD at 2 years) in high-loss adolescents, with partial catch-up after stopping and no fracture signal yet. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added adolescent BMD language to the semaglutide label in 2035 and requires a 5-year extension; pediatric societies advise DEXA at baseline and year two.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imported or counterfeit users rose from ≈7.1M to ≈12.1M. No contamination cluster on the 2033 scale. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls rose another ~25%, mostly dosing errors with Indian 50 mg tablets taken alongside branded starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Seizures and import alerts continue; Safe Pens bill still stalled; individuals still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed fakes are now a large share of parcel seizures, with 0–300% of labelled content. Fakes of 'Unhooked' and 'Quiet' branded tablets appeared in 2036.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy seal; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. NAION and anhedonia-related inactivity are both cited cofactors.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated in over-50s cut off by the 2035–36 employer retreat. DEXA cohorts show more visceral fat and less lean mass at the same weight after repeated cycles.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint endocrine/obesity society guidance (2035) recommends against stopping without a resistance-training plan; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting HR rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial interim analysis in 2036 found no excess MACE.

safety_ledger.effect: Thiamine deficiency and malnutrition in heavy drinkers on AUD treatment
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Case series of Wernicke encephalopathy and severe malnutrition in AUD users whose food intake fell further on the drug while they kept drinking. Small absolute numbers, and probably under-recognised in telehealth and import users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: AUD label recommends nutritional assessment and thiamine supplementation; ASAM guidance; no Warning.

food_and_beverage.state: With about 36.5% of adults on the drug, salty snacks fall ~4–5% a year and confectionery ~6%. Two PE-owned candy portfolios sold brands to Mexican and Turkish buyers for export markets. Protein and 'bone-forward' dairy lead at the premium end. Discount grocers in Dayton and Phoenix's west side sell calorie-dense value packs to people who just lost employer coverage. The industry has adapted to two customers: the coached user buying grams and the off-drug household buying calories.

alcohol.state: Spirits volume fell ~7% in 2035 and ~8% in 2036 as AUD prescribing went on-label and EAPs refer routinely. Two mid-size distillers merged, and craft distillery closures are concentrated in Kentucky and Texas. State alcohol excise receipts fell enough that four state budget offices cite them. Non-alcoholic formats grew to roughly a tenth of beer volume. On-premise bars in high-uptake suburbs are converting to 'NA-forward' menus.

restaurants.state: Traffic roughly flat. Spend per cover in high-uptake suburbs is down ~12% from 2028, with the drop now driven by drinks as much as food. Bar revenue at casual dining chains is the line analysts watch. Value buffets in non-expansion rural states keep recovering among off-drug families.

apparel.state: Class sizing is industry standard. 'Structured' premium lines tailored for trained, medicated bodies, against 'cycle' and elastic ranges at discount chains. A national chain reports that its Phoenix Scottsdale and Maryvale stores now stock almost non-overlapping size curves. Plus-size mid-market keeps shrinking; resale for cycling bodies keeps growing.

fitness.state: Growing at the top, thinning in the middle. DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' expand. Mid-market gyms lose members as employer coverage drops and wellness dollars move to adherence-verification vendors. The binding constraint is still staff qualified for older lifters.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell from 64% to 46%. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiac, OSA, CKD and, under mental-health parity, AUD codes. Remaining obesity coverage is gated and increasingly adherence-verified by connected caps under the 2035 wellness rule. Pharmacy trend slowed to ~+6% as weight volume left the plans. Diagnosis-coding audits for AUD claims are a new PBM product line. Life insurers price untreated BMI and now ask about AUD prescriptions, which creates disclosure friction.

pharma.state: Volume up ~25% over two years with flat net prices. Novo leads US scripts on the 50 mg pill and the AUD label. Lilly leads revenue on tirzepatide and retatrutide. Amgen's MariTide grows in the coached tier. Generic entry is blocked by injunction. Telehealth brands built on $149 starters are the fastest-growing channel. Indian makers dominate ex-US volume and the parcel trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, more legibly than in 2034. Trained shoulders and DEXA-stable lean mass read as top third and coached injectable. A lean, soft 'pill body' reads as middle: the 50 mg pill, cash or AUD-coded. Fresh regain over thin arms reads as someone whose plan dropped obesity coverage in 2035, or as an import user. Weight no longer separates classes. Composition and its stability do.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use converges in rates (31.5% bottom vs 41% top) and diverges in bodies. The demographic most visibly sorted in 2036 is middle-income men 30–49 in logistics and retail management in Columbus and Phoenix. Their employers dropped obesity coverage, so those with diabetes or AUD codes stayed on and those without went to imports or off. Within one warehouse shift you can see who has a code.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm among users. The bigger 2036 change is drinking: office happy hours have become 'NA hours', wedding bars are halved, and toasts are made with seltzer. Sunday full-table dinners and church potlucks persist as heritage and as where off-drug families eat, especially in Memphis and Houston.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'AUD treatment' to their regimen field after users began listing it. 'Coached' is read as money. 'Unmedicated' and 'still drinks' have become a combined niche identity. Advice columns field complaints about partners who became 'nice but absent' after starting.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of every kind is now treated as something managed: food, drink, wagers, carts. Among the insured, wanting things intensely carries a faint diagnostic tinge. The backlash coalition of fat-acceptance groups, some evangelical pastors and 'unmedicated' artists has grown a little. It now argues about desire as much as body size.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled Oct 2035: ~4.8% vs ~2.1% placebo at standard weight doses; ~2.5% vs ~2.0% at low oral starter doses, which is not distinct; ~12% observational at 12 mg retatrutide. Of ≈100.7M users, ≈8.5M are on top-dose triple or dual regimens, implying ~600k excess cases there. The rest of the 2.5–3M implied excess is spread across standard doses. The ≈7.2M 'calm/focus/unhooked' subscribers mostly take starter doses, where the label shows little measurable blunting. Their brands now cite that as reassurance even though they are selling a quieter mind. Counterfeit tablets add unknown exposure.
interior_life.framing: Feature in retail, adverse reaction in the label, treatment in psychiatry. Quiet, Even and Unhooked still charge $149–199 on starter doses. Their onboarding now shows the NAION warning and the anhedonia table, and a 2036 Even campaign reads 'Less noise. Measured.' Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. AUD patients say 'the quiet'. Users who dislike it say 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Many employers that dropped obesity coverage kept $149 'focus' stipends in lifestyle accounts, because they are cheaper. HR also uses the AUD benefit as a performance tool: EAP referral is now a standard step before discipline for alcohol-related incidents in manufacturing and transport. Sales and hospitality staff dose down before peak seasons. Unions now bargain over whether adherence-verified caps can feed wellness premiums and whether anhedonia-related stops count as non-adherence.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' is a marketing genre. 'Written unmedicated' is a badge in Nashville and on comedy tours, and a 2036 festival hit is a documentary about a sober-by-pill bar band. Sportsbook handle growth in New Jersey and Ohio slowed sharply. Operators fund 'responsible gaming' referrals to telehealth prescribers, and critics call this shedding their least profitable compulsive customers while keeping the rest. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing among users who want to feel something on purpose.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose, indication and the anhedonia table. Couples counselling increasingly involves one partner treated for drinking or gambling who is 'easier and further away'. Dose-holiday weekends remain common. Some AUD patients are told not to take them.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 campaign is about price and access. Both parties attack the generic injunction, and populists attack employers for 'taking the pill away'. Alcohol-state delegations from Kentucky, Tennessee and Texas resist Medicaid SUD expansion for the AUD indication over excise losses. A small bipartisan group asks the FTC to look at gambling operators' referral partnerships. No federal law passed.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding. It labelled anhedonia class-wide with prevalence, approved the semaglutide AUD indication on two phase 3 trials, approved survodutide for MASH, and added adolescent BMD language. It still brings no individual import prosecutions. Congress has passed no importation or authentication law. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Part D obesity benefit is unchanged at $199 and $50. The 90% Medicaid match continues for 31 states plus DC. AUD-indicated use is covered under Medicaid SUD benefits and Part D. MHPAEA parity rules mean commercial plans covering SUD medications must cover the AUD indication on comparable terms, which is now the main non-diabetic route into employer coverage. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA, 90-day bone pause, two misses suspend for 6 months. Indiana and Arkansas 12-month lockouts were upheld by the Seventh Circuit in 2035. The April 2035 tri-agency (HHS/DOL/Treasury) wellness rule lets outcome-based programs use pharmacy PDC and connected-cap adherence data within the existing 30% surcharge limit. Texas and Georgia state-employee plans now require connected-cap adherence for incretin coverage and premium tiers. The AUD benefit carries its own conditioning: many plans require quarterly PEth blood tests to continue.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide. Large fleets do visual-field checks for medicated drivers over 50. After the AUD approval, FMCSA issued guidance that AUD-indicated incretins do not themselves disqualify drivers. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world and the ≈12.1M-user US gray market. Section 232 tariffs remain. The Telangana import alert is still a bilateral irritant, and India cites the US generic injunction as evidence of protectionism in trade talks. Canada's generic oral semaglutide feeds cross-border pharmacy trips from Michigan and Vermont.

events.event: Novo Nordisk files a supplemental application for the 50 mg Wegovy pill and the 2.4 mg injection to treat moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder, citing two phase 3 trials showing a 30–35% reduction in heavy-drinking days versus placebo. By the next year the pill becomes the most-dispensed incretin in the US

HHS, Labor and Treasury finalise a wellness-program rule allowing outcome-based programs to use pharmacy adherence and connected-cap data inside the existing 30% surcharge limit. Texas and Georgia state-employee plans adopt connected-cap requirements for incretin coverage within months

A Delaware federal judge grants a preliminary injunction on a later-expiring semaglutide formulation and device patent, blocking rival generic launches as their mid-2035 settlement date arrives. Portal prices stay where the 2033 increase left them

FDA adds reduced interest or pleasure (anhedonia) to the Adverse Reactions section of every GLP-1 receptor agonist label, with a prevalence table: about 4.8% versus 2.1% on placebo at weight-loss doses. Within weeks, telehealth 'calm' brands advertise that the label shows little effect at their starter doses

FDA approves semaglutide for alcohol use disorder. Major employers had already dropped obesity coverage in the 2035 and 2036 plan years, so national coverage falls to 46%. Mental-health parity now obliges those same plans to cover the drug for drinking, and PBMs launch AUD coding audits

An American Psychiatric Association practice guideline endorses GLP-1 drugs as a second-line option for gambling disorder and compulsive buying. Unhooked launches a $179 'bet-quiet' tier the same month, and sportsbooks in New Jersey and Ohio begin referral partnerships

open_tensions: Employers dropped obesity coverage but must cover the same pill for drinking under parity law. The resulting coding route, contested by PBM audits and PEth-test conditions, decides who in the middle third stays on. Nobody knows how much 'AUD' prescribing is really weight prescribing.

Anhedonia is now labelled at ~4.8% at weight doses and near placebo at starter doses, and calm brands use that table as advertising. The ≈7.2M subscribers and ≈1.2M compulsion-guideline users are being treated for desire itself, and no long-term randomised data exist for that use.

The generic injunction awaits the Federal Circuit while ≈12.1M Americans use imports and pressed tablets with no authentication law. A ruling either way in 2037 reprices the market, the gray trade and Medicare's fixed $199 rate all at once.

The 2035 tri-agency rule lets connected-cap adherence data feed premiums. Unions, disability advocates and privacy groups are challenging whether anhedonia- or NAION-related stops can be counted as non-adherence, and Medicare's ≈20,000 excess hip fractures a year are still unscored.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The 'Safe Pens' authentication bill is still stalled; Congress has passed no importation or authentication law, and individual import users are still not prosecuted.

prose.headline: The Pill for Wanting: one in three Americans now takes the same drug, for their waist, their whiskey or their bets
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 a little over a third of American adults take an incretin drug, and a growing share of them are not taking it for their weight. The fifty-milligram Wegovy pill, which matched the weekly shot two years ago, is now the most-dispensed drug in the class. Since January it has also been an approved treatment for alcohol use disorder. Since May, the country's psychiatrists have listed it as a reasonable second try for people who cannot stop betting or buying.

Prices did not fall. The rival generics that were due in mid-2035 met a Delaware injunction on a formulation patent, so the portal prices set after the 2033 increase still hold. Medicare's statutory rate of $199 has not moved either. Employers, carrying the gap, kept leaving. Fewer than half now cover the drug for weight. What remains is diabetes, heart, sleep apnea and kidney coverage, with obesity coverage left in a minority of plans that watch adherence through connected pill caps under a federal wellness rule finalised in 2035. Texas and Georgia run their state workers' plans the same way.

Then the alcohol approval opened a door the employers had just closed. Mental-health parity law says a plan that covers addiction medicines must cover them fairly, so the same plans that dropped the drug for weight must now pay for it for drinking. Benefits consultants call this the AUD door. Pharmacy managers sell coding audits and quarterly blood tests for alcohol markers to keep it narrow. In the middle third of incomes, whether you stay on depends more and more on what is written in your chart.

Almost everyone priced out found another source. About twelve million people use imported or counterfeit product, mostly Indian generic pills and pens, and some Chinese vials. Another seven million pay $149 to $199 a month for low-dose subscriptions sold as calm, focus or, since the gambling guideline, quiet around the betting app. Bars in the suburbs have become seltzer rooms. Spirits volume fell by about a fifth over two years, and Kentucky's budget office now writes about excise receipts the way Appalachia once wrote about coal.

In October 2035 the side effect people had argued about for years got a number. The FDA's class label now lists reduced interest or pleasure at about 4.8 percent at weight-loss doses, against 2.1 percent on placebo, and close to placebo at the starter doses the calm brands sell. The calm brands put that table in their advertising. The label is accurate and so is the ad, and what they are selling is a quieter version of wanting.

Bodies sort by income more legibly than before. In Phoenix and Columbus a warehouse shift is a lesson in insurance design. Men with a diabetes or alcohol code are steady and lean, and men without one are regaining over thin arms or ordering from Hyderabad. Coached injectable users in Scottsdale keep their muscle. Older users on Medicare keep breaking hips, about twenty thousand excess a year, in a part of the budget that never pays for the pill.

The campaign this autumn is about price, the injunction and employers taking the pill away. Nobody is running on the question the label has started to answer, which is what it means for a third of a country to want things a little less. The Federal Circuit's ruling on the injunction is due next year.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marcus Bell twists the cap at 5:40 and it chirps green. The phone says ninety-four percent this quarter. His wellness tier holds at ninety. The bottle says Wegovy, fifty milligrams. The chart says alcohol use disorder, moderate. His copay is forty dollars because of a law about fairness he has never read.

On the drive to the distribution centre outside Dayton he passes the liquor store where he used to stop on Fridays. It sells kombucha now, in the front window.

At break Troy is eating a gas-station burrito and two donuts. Troy's plan dropped him in January. Troy doesn't drink. "Should've been a drunk," Troy says, and they both laugh, and then they don't.

The kiosk by the time clock asks Marcus to step on. He steps on.

After shift the crew goes to Hank's. Marcus orders the NA amber and it tastes like the idea of beer. The Bengals are on. Somebody's parlay hits and the table yells. Marcus feels the yell arrive a second after everyone else's, as if from another room. The Medication Guide calls this reduced interest. He read the table once. Four point eight percent.

At home Danielle is in the bathroom with a pen from a padded envelope with Indian stamps. She reads the lot number aloud against a list on her phone. Clean.

Their daughter Kayla, eleven, is drawing at the kitchen table. "Dad, look." It's a horse, and it's good.

"That's good, baby," he says, and he means it, and he waits to feel it, and he keeps looking at the horse while he waits.
